an7.42:3.1: “This morning, sir, I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
an7.42:3.3: “It’s too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthī.
an7.42:3.4: Why don’t I visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?”
an7.42:3.5: So I went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.
an7.42:3.6: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, I sat down to one side.
an7.42:3.7: Now at that time, sir, while those wanderers of other religions were sitting together this discussion came up among them:
an7.42:3.8: “Reverends, anyone who lives the full and pure spiritual life for twelve years is qualified to be called a ‘graduate mendicant’.”
an7.42:3.9: Sir, I neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions.
an7.42:3.10: Neither approving nor rejecting it, I rose from my seat and left, thinking:
an7.42:3.11: “‘I will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.’”
